newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian man has gallbladder "boulder" removed.
newsitem.headline: Colombian man has gallbladder "boulder" removed.

text.p: A Colombian man was recovering in the Caribbean port city of Barranquilla on Friday after surgery in which doctors removed what news reports described as a massive gall stone weighing 4.4 pounds (2 kg).
The flesh-coloured medical equivalent of a "boulder," shown on television news programmes, was removed from a dazed-looking Ricardo Roncallo, who may well earn a place in the Guinness record book.
"I imagined something much smaller," Roncallo, 28, told the Noticiero Nacional TV news.

Officials at the Hospital General in Barranquilla where the operation was performed on Thursday could not be reached for comment. But a report in Colombia's leading newspaper, El Tiempo, quoted urologist Alberto Barros Hernandez, who operated on Roncallo, as confirming that the 5.7 inch (14.5 cm) growth removed from his gallbladder was a stone and not a tumour.
Barros said a book published by the Spanish Urological Association mentioned a case in 1975 involving a stone weighing 17 ounces (485 grams) but he said Roncallo's may be the biggest ever discovered.
"Its growth was similar to that of an onion, in layers," he told El Tiempo.
